newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: New York to resume Corimon ADRs Monday.
newsitem.headline: New York to resume Corimon ADRs Monday.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange will resume trading of Venezuelan paints company Corimon American Depository Receipts (ADR) July 28, the company said Friday.

Following a recent restructuring of the company's stock agreed last Monday each ADR will be equivalent to 250 ordinary shares compared to 35 shares when trading was suspended in early 1996, Corimon said in a release.
Corimon shareholders agreed late Monday to convert its preferred B shares to A shares at the rate of 10:13.5.
The company's B shares are the result of debt/equity swap with creditors, used to bail out the company when it was brought down last year by its California subsidiary Standard Brand Paints.
Trading on both the NYSE and Caracas bolsa's was suspended in February 1996. Local trade re-opened October 1996.

In the company's annual general meeting late Monday, shareholders also approved a capital increase of up to 4.3 billion bolivars ($8.7 million) through the issue of up to 427 million B shares at a nominal value of 10 bolivars.

Analysts credit the company with emerging relatively quickly from a vast and painful restructuring process that saw creditors, holding debts totaling $100.8 million, take control of over 80 percent of the company's equity last year.
